speaker_role: independent counselor / former admissions professional (former director of MBA admissions and financial aid at Wharton; now hosts a college admissions podcast/consultancy)
commercial_incentive: hosts the 'Admittedly' podcast/brand and appears to run a paid admissions-advising practice; episode functions as content marketing for that brand
key_insights: For Yale's 'up to three prospective academic areas' question, advises listing one area clearly consistent with the rest of the application plus one or two genuinely curious 'left field' areas rather than forcing total consistency

For the 'topic or idea that excites you' prompt, advises picking something the student can speak passionately about and tying it to one of the chosen academic areas, even if it stems from an unrelated hobby
For the 'why Yale' reflection, advises grounding the answer in specific, personal detail about how the student would actually live and engage on campus rather than generic praise of the school
Warns against answering all four short 35-word questions in an overly academic/goal-focused way, since it makes the applicant look one-dimensional and not 'fun'
For the 'influence' question, cautions against defaulting to 'a student I mentored' since it's a very common, low-differentiation answer unless given a truly personal, unique treatment
For the prompt about something not covered elsewhere in the application, recommends using it for a fun, humanizing personal detail rather than another achievement

For the 'opposing view' essay option, warns against a confrontational or highly political topic, especially given current campus sensitivities, and notes the essay can instead show the student changing their own mind
For the 'community' essay, stresses defining community broadly/personally and using it to convey background and the kind of diversity the student would add to the class
specific_numbers_or_facts: States the four short-answer questions are capped at 200 characters (about 35 words), per the speaker
States the longer essay option is capped at 400 words, per the speaker
notable_or_distinctive: Distinctive for being a prompt-by-prompt strategic breakdown of Yale's exact current application questions, rather than generic essay-writing advice.
reliability_notes: Speaker is a paid admissions consultant/podcast host actively promoting his own brand, so advice carries promotional framing; his stated professional background is MBA admissions (Wharton), not undergraduate admissions, though the content targets undergraduate Yale applicants; auto-captions are clean.
